happened: Group 2 built an automated workflow that wakes when an email request lands, reads what is being asked, uses email and the CRM, names a specialist, and hands off to an associate who is not out. The instruction is not to assume, and to identify the client, the policy, and the ask.
issue: The next person still has to guess who owns it next. An associate who is not out is a staffing rule, not a named owner. The instruction also never states the job to be done (a reviewed inforce illustration) or that the email is from a wealth strategist, not the client.
why: The outcome is a simple document: job in plain words, the tools needed, and a real person who owns it next. Tools are fine. The job is a fragment, not the job to be done. Handoff is not a person. Someone who was not in the group still has to guess who they hand this to and what file they owe.

board.container: Automated Workflow — if this, then that
board.instruction: Never want it to assume. Must identfy, client policy, the ask
board.handoff: An associate who is not out
